label: Possible heritages
summary: The list of heritages the culture divergence window offers.
details: Going by its name and its use as the list source of a widget in the divergence window (gui/window_diverge_culture.gui), it fills a list with the heritages (the ancestry group of a culture) that can be picked there.

label: Possible languages
summary: The list of languages the culture divergence window offers.
details: Going by its name and its use as the list source of a widget in the divergence window (gui/window_diverge_culture.gui), it fills a list with the languages that can be picked there.

label: Possible martial customs
summary: The list of martial customs the culture divergence window offers.
details: Going by its name and its use as the list source of a widget in the divergence window (gui/window_diverge_culture.gui), it fills a list with the martial customs (how the culture fights) that can be picked there.

label: Selected tradition
summary: The tradition currently selected in the culture divergence window.
details: Vanilla compares it with a tradition entry (ObjectsEqual) to decide whether a part of that entry is visible, so that part shows only for the selected tradition.

label: Selected tradition group
summary: Probably the group of traditions currently selected in the culture divergence window.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Tradition cost

fields.text: The tradition whose cost is wanted.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example CultureTradition.Self

label: Tradition cost breakdown
summary: The text that explains how the cost of a tradition is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a tradition entry in the culture divergence window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition whose cost is explained.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example CultureTradition.Self

label: Tradition group
summary: A named group of traditions of the culture divergence window.
details: Vanilla asks for the groups called 'realm' and 'combat' and uses them as the data context of a section. It also asks the group for its category and makes that the shown category when the window opens.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the group.
fields.values: a text such as 'realm' or 'combat'

label: Traditions list
summary: The list of traditions shown in the culture divergence window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list source of a widget in the window; each entry is one tradition.

label: Vassal conversion window
summary: Probably the part of the divergence window that deals with converting vassals.
details: Going by its name and its use as the data context of a section of the culture divergence window (gui/window_diverge_culture.gui).

label: Has aesthetic
summary: Whether the given culture aesthetic is chosen in the divergence window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the down (pressed) state of the button that picks an aesthetic, which also calls SetAesthetic on click.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The aesthetic to check.
fields.values: a culture aesthetic, for example CultureAesthetics.Self

label: Has pillar
summary: Whether the given culture pillar is chosen in the divergence window.
details: Vanilla uses it for the down (pressed) state of pillar buttons and for the visibility of another widget, next to SetPillar on click.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The pillar to check.
fields.values: a culture pillar, for example CulturePillar.Self

label: Has tradition
summary: Probably whether the given tradition is part of the culture being diverged.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the hybridization window has a function of the same name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition to check.
fields.values: a culture tradition

label: Has tradition category
summary: Probably whether the given tradition category is the one the window currently shows.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed look and the visibility of the category buttons, next to SetTraditionCategory. The exact meaning is read from that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The category to check.
fields.values: a tradition category, for example TraditionGrouping.GetCategory

label: On edit collective noun
summary: Runs when the player edits the collective noun text box of the new culture.
details: Vanilla attaches it to the text-edited event of a text box in the culture divergence window. It returns nothing.

label: On edit name
summary: Runs when the player edits the name text box of the new culture.
details: Vanilla attaches it to the text-edited event of a text box in the culture divergence window. It returns nothing.

label: On edit prefix
summary: Runs when the player edits the prefix text box of the new culture.
details: Vanilla attaches it to the text-edited event of a text box in the culture divergence window. It returns nothing.

label: Replace tradition
summary: Probably replaces a tradition of the culture with the one that was clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click on a tradition entry, passing that entry. Going by its name; the input does not show which tradition is removed. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition to put in.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example CultureTradition.Self

label: Divergence window itself
summary: The culture divergence window itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Going by its name; vanilla never uses it on this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set aesthetic
summary: Chooses the given aesthetic for the new culture.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click on an aesthetic button. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The aesthetic to choose.
fields.values: a culture aesthetic, for example CultureAesthetics.Self

label: Set color
summary: Applies the color the player picked to the new culture.
details: Vanilla calls it from the color-edited event of a color picker in the divergence window. It returns nothing and takes no argument.

label: Set pillar
summary: Chooses the given culture pillar for the new culture.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click on a pillar button. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The pillar to choose.
fields.values: a culture pillar, for example CulturePillar.Self

label: Set selected tradition
summary: Makes the given tradition the selected one in the divergence window.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click on a tradition entry; GetSelectedTradition then returns it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tradition to select.
fields.values: a culture tradition, for example CultureTradition.Self

label: Set tradition category
summary: Switches the divergence window to the given tradition category.
details: Vanilla calls it when the window opens (with the category of the 'realm' group) and on a click on a category button. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The category to show.
fields.values: a tradition category, for example TraditionGrouping.GetCategory

label: Has icon
summary: Probably whether the doctrine has an icon.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; other types have a function of the same name.

label: Is valid
summary: Probably whether the doctrine is a valid, existing one.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of parts of notification templates; the name IsValid appears on many types.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the doctrine is shown.
details: Vanilla combines it with the faith having the doctrine to decide what the knights window shows.

label: Localize
summary: Probably the doctrine's text for a given localization key.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the lines with the same name use the general Localize function.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented.
fields.values: unknown

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the doctrine into a script scope that GUI scripted checks can work with.
details: Vanilla adds it under the name 'doctrine' to the scope given to a scripted GUI check in the rite creation window.

label: Doctrine itself
summary: The doctrine itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to checks such as whether a faith has the doctrine, or whether the player knows it, and to the doctrine cost in the rite creation window.

label: Domicile access
summary: A GUI function that hands back the domicile itself.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it on this type and the game documents nothing more.

label: Build building
summary: A command that builds the given building in the domicile.
details: Vanilla sends it with PostCommand on a click and checks it with IsValidCommand to enable the button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The building to build.
fields.values: a domicile building, for example DomicileBuilding.Self

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Vanilla passes the domicile window here; the input does not say what it is used for.
fields.values: for example DomicileWindow.Self

label: Can move
summary: Whether the domicile can be moved.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a widget in the map icon layer and in the domicile window.

label: Can move to
summary: Whether the domicile can be moved to the given province.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a widget in the county view.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The target province.
fields.values: a province, for example Province.Self

label: Can upgrade main
summary: Whether the domicile's main building can be upgraded.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it for the visibility of widgets in the outliner and the map icon layer, and combines it with IsConstructing in another check.
